applies_to: Yaskawa HV600 HVAC fan and pump drives (HV60U, 208 V and 480 V class) using the built-in RS-485 port with H5-08 set to BACnet.
summary: The HV600 has BACnet MS/TP built into its RS-485 terminals (TB6); set H5-08 = 3 to select it. The fixed object list covers analog and digital I/O, run/fault/reset and emergency-override commands, frequency and PID setpoint references, output and energy monitors, fault codes and a long set of status flags. AV29/AV30 give indirect access to any drive parameter by Modbus register number.
firmware: PICS lists application software VSEA010xx, firmware revision 2.01
notes: Objects marked Not Used (AI3-AI5, AV31, AV32, AV34, AV41, BI10-BI27, BI30, BV58, BV59, BV61, BV62) are left out. The manual prints BI17 as B17.
Each object has a long name and a shorter network display name; the long name is listed and the display name is given as 'Shown as' in the description.
AV1, AV4 and AV5 are packed command words; the manual says not to use AV1 with BV1-BV11 or AV5, AV4 with BO1-BO3 or BV12, or AV5 with AV1, BO4 or BV9-BV11.
Frequency units follow the o1-03 display setting.
AV29/AV30 with BV55/BV56 read and write drive parameters that are not in the object list.
Each description gives the drive Modbus register where the manual lists one (hex).

source.title: YASKAWA HV600 Drive Technical Reference (section 6.3, BACnet Communications)

integration.summary: Set H5-08 = 3 (BACnet), the MS/TP address in H5-01, the baud rate in H5-02, H5-12 = 0 and the device instance in H5-14/H5-15, then cycle power or set H5-20 = 1. Set b1-01 = 2 and b1-02 = 2 (or an AUTO + serial run setting) so the network supplies the frequency reference and run command. Write BV1 RUN FWD and AV2 Frequency Command, read BV13/BV16 and AV10/AV12/AV13, and reset faults with BV4.
integration.enable: Set b1-01 Frequency Reference Selection 1 = 2 (Serial Communications) and b1-02 Run Command Selection 1 = 2 (Serial Communications); b1-02 = 7, 8 or 9 combine the keypad AUTO command with terminal, serial or option run. With H5-12 = 0, BV1 runs forward and BV2 runs reverse. Monitoring, parameter access, fault reset and the multi-function inputs work whatever b1-01/b1-02 are set to.
integration.heartbeat: H5-05 = 1 (default) turns on CE detection: if the drive gets no data from the master for H5-09 (0.0-10.0 s, default 2.0 s) it acts per H5-04: 0 ramp to stop, 1 coast, 2 fast stop (C1-09), 3 alarm only and keep running (default), 4 run at the H5-34 speed (H5-35 can then coast to stop with a CE fault after a set time).
integration.remote_sensors: AV3 PID Setpoint lets the BMS write the PID setpoint (0-100 %); BO4 Ref Sel: PID Setpoint (or AV5 bit 1) selects it. The object list has no writable PID feedback.
setup: H5-08 = 3 selects BACnet; H5-01 is the MS/TP address (default 1FH) and must be unique.
H5-02 sets the baud rate; the PICS lists 9600, 19200, 38400 and 76800 bps (default setting 3 = 9600 bps).
H5-03 sets parity (default none); data is 8 bits with 1 stop bit.
Device instance = H5-14 (low word) + H5-15 (high word), in hex; default 1. Example: 1234 is H5-14 = 04D2, H5-15 = 0000.
Wire to TB6 (D+, D-, AC); DIP switch S2 = ON enables termination on the end drives only.
Up to 127 drives per MS/TP segment; the device object name (20 characters) is writable and takes effect after a power cycle.
gotchas: H5-04 defaults to Alarm Only, so the drive keeps running when BACnet traffic stops.
BV56 Parameter Enter writes EEPROM (rated about 100,000 writes); don't use it cyclically.
Don't mix the packed words (AV1, AV4, AV5) with the single-bit BV/BO objects they duplicate.
Serial inputs and the S1-S7 terminals are ORed together.
Frequency objects use the o1-03 display units, which are not always Hz.
